speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with a limp and localized pain, but no fever. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly where it hurts when you walk?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. The child complains of pain in his left knee, but denies any recent trauma or injury. He has no fever or other systemic symptoms. Nutrition and developmental milestones are appropriate for age.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the pain is in the knee but the limp suggests a hip issue, does moving your hip—such as bending it or rotating your leg—make the pain worse? Also, has anyone noticed any swelling or warmth around the knee or hip area?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain localized to the left knee. I also have Limping favoring left leg, No fever, No systemic symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Synovitis of the Hip (referred knee pain). The clinical picture of a limp with localized knee pain in a 7-year-old male, lacking fever or trauma, is classic for transient synovitis where hip pathology refers pain to the knee.
